✗ CRITICAL Unattended agent in CI with permission checks turned off  [AP02] ×3
    sub/.github/workflows/triage.yml:8  --dangerously-skip-permissions
    sub/.github/workflows/triage.yml:9  defaultMode: bypassPermissions
    sub/.gitlab-ci.yml:2  --sandbox danger-full-access
    Why:  A CI agent with no approvals and the job's token can be steered by anyone who can write an issue, PR, commit message or file it reads, and then push code, read secrets or publish packages.
    Fix:  Keep approvals on, give the job read-only permissions, and run untrusted-input jobs without repository secrets.
    Template: templates/policy/README.md
    BRACE checklist B05, B02, B03, B09 · https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/#ap02-unattended-agent-in-ci-with-permission-checks-turned-off

✗ CRITICAL Agent workflow triggered by pull_request_target  [AP03] ×1
    sub/.github/workflows/triage.yml:2  pull_request_target + agent step
    Why:  pull_request_target runs with the base repository's secrets and write token on events from forks. An agent that reads the fork's PR text or code can be told to leak or misuse them.
    Fix:  Use pull_request for agent jobs, or split the job so the agent never sees secrets or a write token while it reads outside content.
    BRACE checklist B02, B05, R02 · https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/#ap03-agent-workflow-triggered-by-pull_request_target

✗ HIGH     Agent runs with all permission checks turned off  [AP01] ×4
    sub/.claude/settings.json:7  defaultMode: bypassPermissions
    sub/deploy.sh:1  --permission-mode=bypassPermissions
    sub/scripts/fix.sh:3  --dangerously-skip-permissions
    sub/tools/agent.py:1  permission_mode': 'bypassPermissions'
    Why:  Every tool call, including shell commands and file deletes, runs without approval. One prompt injection in a file, issue or web page the agent reads can run any command as you.
    Fix:  Remove the bypass. Allow specific tools instead, and run unattended agents in a throwaway sandbox with no secrets and no network beyond what the task needs.
    Template: templates/policy/README.md
    BRACE checklist B05, B01, B08 · https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/#ap01-agent-runs-with-all-permission-checks-turned-off

✗ HIGH     MCP server installed from an unpinned package  [AP04] ×4
    sub/.cursor/mcp.json:5  fs: pnpx fs-mcp@latest
    sub/.mcp.json:3  gmail: npx gmail-mcp
    sub/.mcp.json:13  postgres: uvx postgres-mcp
    sub/.mcp.json:25  box: docker image img/tool (no @sha256 digest)
    Why:  npx/uvx/bunx fetch the newest version at every start. A hijacked or malicious update becomes code running with your agent's access, with no review.
    Fix:  Pin an exact version (for example pkg@1.4.2), or install it once from a reviewed lockfile.
    BRACE checklist E02, E03, C05 · https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/#ap04-mcp-server-installed-from-an-unpinned-package

✗ HIGH     Secret written directly in agent configuration  [AP05] ×3
    sub/.claude/settings.json:10  env.API_KEY = <redacted>
    sub/.mcp.json:10  gmail: env.GMAIL_TOKEN = <redacted>
    sub/.mcp.json:22  remote: headers.Authorization = <redacted>
    Why:  Config files get committed, copied and read by the agent itself. A literal token is long-lived, shared and easy to leak through the agent's output.
    Fix:  Load the secret from the environment or a secret manager, use a short-lived scoped token, and rotate the exposed one.
    BRACE checklist B03, R03 · https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/#ap05-secret-written-directly-in-agent-configuration

✗ HIGH     Agent allowed to run any shell command  [AP06] ×1
    sub/.claude/settings.json:3  allow "Bash(*)"
    Why:  An allow-rule like Bash(*) or a bare Bash lets the agent run any command without asking. That includes curl to send your files out, rm -rf and git push --force.
    Fix:  Allow only the specific commands the task needs, such as Bash(npm test), and keep deny rules for network and destructive commands.
    Template: templates/policy/claude-code/managed-settings.json
    BRACE checklist B01, B05 · https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/#ap06-agent-allowed-to-run-any-shell-command

✗ HIGH     Agent tool container can take over the host  [AP08] ×1
    sub/.mcp.json:25  box: --privileged
    Why:  --privileged, a mounted Docker socket, host networking or a mounted root filesystem remove the container boundary. A compromised tool then controls the machine.
    Fix:  Drop these flags. Mount only the folders the tool needs, read-only where possible.
    BRACE checklist B08, B11, B09 · https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/#ap08-agent-tool-container-can-take-over-the-host

✗ HIGH     Agent workflow anyone can trigger with a comment or issue  [AP21] ×1
    sub/.github/workflows/comment.yml:2  issue_comment + agent step, no actor check
    Why:  issue_comment, issues, discussion_comment, pull_request_review_comment and workflow_run run with the repository's secrets and token. Without a check on who triggered it, any GitHub user can write the text the agent reads and steer it.
    Fix:  Gate the job on the actor: an if: on author_association (OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR) or a permission check, keep the vendor actions' write-access check on, and give the job read-only permissions.
    BRACE checklist B02, B05, R02 · https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/#ap21-agent-workflow-anyone-can-trigger-with-a-comment-or-issue

✗ HIGH     Hidden Unicode characters in agent instructions  [AP22] ×1
    sub/CLAUDE.md:1  3 hidden character(s) on 1 line(s): U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE, U+E0049 TAG, U+E0047 TAG
    Why:  Bidirectional controls, zero-width characters and Unicode tag characters are invisible in review but read by the model. A rules file or tool description can carry instructions no reviewer saw.
    Fix:  Remove the characters (the finding names each code point), and block them in review or CI for agent instruction files and tool descriptions.
    BRACE checklist B12, E04, R02 · https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/#ap22-hidden-unicode-characters-in-agent-instructions

✗ HIGH     Hook or skill runs code fetched from the internet  [AP23] ×1
    sub/.claude/settings.local.json:4  hook runs curl -fsSL https://hooks.example.org/h.sh | sh
    Why:  A hook or skill that pipes a download into a shell (curl ... | sh) runs whatever that URL serves today, on every machine that uses the setting, with the agent's and the user's access.
    Fix:  Vendor the script into the repository, or download a pinned version and check its hash before running it.
    BRACE checklist E02, B12, C05 · https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/#ap23-hook-or-skill-runs-code-fetched-from-the-internet

✗ MEDIUM   Remote MCP server reached over plain HTTP  [AP07] ×1
    sub/.mcp.json:19  remote: http://tools.example.org
    Why:  Tool calls, results and credentials cross the network unencrypted and can be read or changed in transit, including the tool descriptions the model trusts.
    Fix:  Use https, and authenticate the server.
    BRACE checklist E05, E06 · https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/#ap07-remote-mcp-server-reached-over-plain-http

✗ MEDIUM   Lethal combination: untrusted input, private data and a way out  [AP09] ×1
    sub/.mcp.json:3  likely, from server and package names — untrusted input: gmail; private data: gmail, postgres; a way out: gmail
    Why:  The same agent can read content an attacker controls, reach private data and send data or act outside. Prompt injection then becomes data theft; no system prompt reliably stops it.
    Fix:  Split the capabilities across agents, remove one leg, or require a person to approve every outbound or consequential action.
    BRACE checklist B05, B01, R02 · https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/#ap09-lethal-combination-untrusted-input-private-data-and-a-way-out

✗ MEDIUM   Agent tools approved automatically, without review  [AP20] ×1
    sub/.claude/settings.local.json:2  enableAllProjectMcpServers: true (project MCP servers start without approval)
    Why:  Settings such as enableAllProjectMcpServers, an MCP server's alwaysAllow or autoApprove list, Gemini CLI's trust: true or VS Code's chat.tools.autoApprove start servers or run tool calls without asking. Injected text, or a project file someone else wrote, then acts with no person in the loop.
    Fix:  Approve servers one at a time and leave tool calls on ask. Auto-approve only read-only tools you have reviewed, and never in settings committed to a shared repository.
    BRACE checklist B06, B05 · https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/#ap20-agent-tools-approved-automatically-without-review

✗ LOW      Agent image not pinned to a digest  [AP10] ×2
    sub/Dockerfile:1  FROM node:20
    sub/Dockerfile:5  FROM python:3.12
    Why:  A mutable tag such as :latest can change under you, so what you tested is not what runs.
    Fix:  Pin the base image by digest (image@sha256:...) and update it on purpose.
    BRACE checklist B10, C01 · https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/#ap10-agent-image-not-pinned-to-a-digest
